answer: Modules placed in a plain Python list are not registered by the framework because the
    list itself is not a module [2]. Consequently, methods like `net.parameters()`,
    `net.to(device)`, and `net.state_dict()` will fail to find or manage these layers, leaving
    them untrained or unsaved [2]. While the forward pass may still execute if the code
    explicitly loops over the list, the optimizer will not receive their parameters for gradient
    updates [3]. This results in a "partly registered" model where only the weights of
    registered outer layers change during training, causing the model to learn incorrectly or
    fail on GPU devices [3].
